public_rationale: Published development and AI fit-out benchmarks support the ordinary claim that large AI data centers require very large capital investments. Cushman & Wakefield's modern-facility benchmark scales to $1.76 billion at 100 MW before the GPU costs identified separately. JLL also reports substantial AI fit-out costs. These records establish the cost scale, not the post's exact project estimates or its conclusions about returns.
limitations: The adjective is qualitative; support applies to the stated ordinary reading.
Benchmarks vary by market, facility design, and hardware.
JLL's fit-out number is an upper-end estimate, not an average.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: AI data centers are extremely expensive.

statement.excerpt: AI data centers are extremely expensive.

our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is that large AI data centers require very large absolute capital investments: millions of dollars per MW and potentially billions at the 100-MW scale discussed in the post.
This does not assert that every facility costs billions, that every project costs exactly $4–5 billion per 100 MW, or that high costs imply unprofitability.
Use 2026 year-to-date cost information through September 29, the latest reportable cost-estimate period before publication.
This is a qualitative industry-cost claim, not a financial result for a named company.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporaneous construction and AI hardware benchmarks establish multimillion-dollar costs per MW and billion-dollar-scale capital requirements for large facilities.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative contemporary costs are materially below that scale, showing that the large AI facilities discussed do not require unusually large absolute capital investments.
